definitions.explanation: The degree of detail visible in an image, whether on a screen, in a photograph, or through an optical instrument. Almost always appears in the compound {解像度|かいぞうど} (resolution as a measurable quantity).

examples.japanese: {解像度|かいぞうど}が{高|たか}い{画像|がぞう}を{選|えら}んだ。
このカメラの{解像度|かいぞうど}はどのくらいですか。
examples.english: What is the resolution of this camera?

examples.japanese: {画面|がめん}の{解像度|かいぞうど}を{上|あ}げると、{文字|もじ}や{写真|しゃしん}がより{鮮明|せんめい}に{表示|ひょうじ}されるが、その{分|ぶん}バッテリーの{消耗|しょうもう}が{早|はや}くなる。
examples.english: Increasing the screen resolution displays text and photos more clearly, but the battery drains faster as a result.

notes:
Composed of {解|かい} (resolve, analyze) and {像|ぞう} (image). In practice, {解像|かいぞう} almost never appears alone — it is nearly always used in the compound {解像度|かいぞうど} (resolution, literally "degree of image resolution"). This is an essential technology term for discussing cameras, displays, printers, and digital media.

Note: the homophone {改造|かいぞう} (remodeling, modification) is a completely different word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高|こう}{解像度|かいぞうど}: high resolution
- {低|てい}{解像度|かいぞうど}: low resolution
- {解像度|かいぞうど}を{上|あ}げる: to increase resolution
- {解像度|かいぞうど}が{低|ひく}い: the resolution is low
- {解像力|かいぞうりょく}: resolving power (optics)

RELATED WORDS:
- {画素|がそ}: pixel — the individual dots that make up a digital image
- {画質|がしつ}: image quality — a broader concept than resolution alone
- {鮮明|せんめい}: clear; sharp — describes the visual result of high resolution
